newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan papers hail pruning of president's power.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan papers hail pruning of president's power.

text.p: Pakistani newspapers on Wednesday welcomed the pruning of presidential powers and said it was a decisive step forward for democracy.
"Political sovereignty is finally back where it belongs -- inside the parliament," said the English-language Muslim in a front-page editorial.

Parliament on Tuesday passed constitutional amendments stripping the president of his powers to sack governments and appoint armed forces chiefs and provincial governors, giving the powers back to the prime minister.
"April 1, 1997, will indeed figure as a momentous day in the chequered history of democracy in Pakistan," the newspaper said.

The bill overwrites clauses of the controversial Eighth Amendment, a relic from the military rule of late president General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq from 1977 to 1988, and used by three presidents to sack four prime ministers in the past eight years.
Current Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif has been sacked from the post once, and his predecessor, Benazir Bhutto, twice.

Under the amendments, dissolution of the National Assembly and subsequent sacking of a prime minister and the appointment of armed forces chiefs and provincial governors by the president will be subject to binding prime ministerial advice.
One amendment also bars provincial governors from dissolving provincial parliaments without binding advice from provincial chief ministers.

"The Eighth Amendment has finally lost its sting. The parliament on Tuesday passed the 13th Amendment Bill, repealing some of the most offensive clauses of the dictatorial instrument," The Frontier Post daily said.
"This represents a decisive step forward for the fledgling democracy in Pakistan."
However, newspapers cautioned Sharif and parliament not to forget their new responsibilities.
"Following the emasculation of the Eighth Amendment, the new government would have to tread carefully," The Frontier Post said. "Which effectively means working responsibly and democratically.
The Lahore-based English-language daily The Nation urged the government and the opposition to cooperate to counter threats to democracy.

"An equally significant implication of the 13th Amendment ...is that a much heavier responsibility will now rest on our politicians and legislators to run the system in a responsible manner and not give adventurers the excuse to push it off the track," it said.
